content: Know thyself, and you will know the universe and the gods.
author: Ancient Greek Proverbs
sourceWork: Gnothi seauton (Γνῶθι σεαυτόν) — Inscribed on the Temple of Apollo at Delphi
explanation: Before exploring galaxies, conquering lands, or analyzing complex systems, the human seeker must confront the primary mystery: the one who is looking. To know your own weaknesses, impulses, divine light, and illusions is the summit of all earthly knowledge.
practicalInsight: Spend five minutes journaling on this single question today: 'Who am I when nobody is watching and I have nothing to prove?'
reflectionPrompt: Are you spending your entire life studying external things while remaining a complete stranger to your own soul?
